raw_case_text: Eleven days after admission, the child's condition was not alleviated. The ECMO support time was quite long, while the lung infection remained serious. The G test value increased (2419.3 pg/mL). The patient underwent bronchoscopy with a collection of BALF for routine examination and mNGS experiment. The smear and culture results were negative, and the mNGS results showed that the level of Pneumocystis infection decreased but CMV levels increased (Table 1). CT showed that both lungs were white with pneumothorax and pleural effusion (Figure 2C and D). Anti-infective treatment with MEM (100 mg Q8H) and CAS (50 mg QOD) was continued to prevent infection. Cefoperazone sodium and sulbactam sodium were administered (SCF, 400 mg Q8H) combined with TMP-SMX tablets (150 mg Q6H). Given that the number of platelets and lymphocytes were low in the patient, acyclovir (10 mg/kg dose Q8H) and IVIG (2.5 g/day) antiviral therapy were added for 2 days. Flow cytometry of peripheral blood cells showed that the CD3+ T cells/lymphocyte level was 52.32% (normal range 58.4-81.56%), and the CD4+ T cells/CD8+ T cells level was 4.2 (normal range 0.80-2.60). The diagnosis of immunodeficiency could not be excluded. After the following few days of treatment, the child was still in critical condition, and the G test value increased more (4138.0 pg/mL). CR showed that the lungs were still exuding severely (Figure 2E and F). The treatment, including ECMO, was suspended upon the request of the family. The child was eventually discharged after consent was obtained. Unfortunately, according to the telephone follow-up one week later, the child died two days later after leaving the hospital.

subjective.chief_complaint: A critically ill pediatric patient on prolonged extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for severe Pneumocystis jirovecii and cytomegalovirus co-infected pneumonia remained in refractory respiratory failure on hospital day 11.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: After 11 days of inpatient treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, caspofungin, meropenem, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for mNGS-confirmed Pneumocystis jirovecii and cytomegalovirus pneumonia, the child's severe pulmonary infection and ECMO dependency failed to improve.
subjective.past_medical_history: Severe Pneumocystis jirovecii and cytomegalovirus pneumonia on prolonged ECMO support; suspected underlying primary immunodeficiency.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent critical respiratory failure.

objective.physical_examination: Critical respiratory failure requiring prolonged ECMO support, complicated by pneumothorax and pleural effusion.
objective.routine_investigations: Hematology: Thrombocytopenia and lymphopenia. Chest radiograph (CR): Persistent severe bilateral pulmonary exudation ('white-out' lungs).
objective.advanced_workup: Serial serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan (G test): Markedly elevated at 2,419.3 pg/mL on day 11, rising further to 4,138.0 pg/mL over the subsequent days. Peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets (flow cytometry): Decreased CD3+ T-cell percentage at 52.32% (normal: 58.4%–81.56%) and elevated CD4+/CD8+ ratio at 4.2 (normal: 0.80–2.60), suggestive of underlying immunodeficiency. Day 11 chest CT: Bilateral 'white-out' lungs complicated by pneumothorax and pleural effusion. Day 11 bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) mNGS: Routine BALF smears and cultures negative; repeat BALF mNGS demonstrated a decreased read count of Pneumocystis jirovecii alongside an increased read count of cytomegalovirus (CMV).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Refractory fatal Pneumocystis jirovecii and cytomegalovirus (CMV) pneumonia complicated by bilateral 'white-out' lungs, pneumothorax, pleural effusion, and prolonged ECMO dependence (with serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan rising to 4,138.0 pg/mL and persistent P. jirovecii and rising CMV reads on day 11 BALF mNGS) in a child with suspected underlying T-cell immunodeficiency. Plan and clinical course: Continued on meropenem (100 mg q8h), caspofungin (50 mg QOD), cefoperazone-sulbactam (400 mg q8h), oral TMP-SMX (150 mg q6h), intravenous acyclovir (10 mg/kg q8h), and IVIG (2.5 g/day for 2 days). Due to worsening refractory respiratory failure and rising beta-D-glucan (4,138.0 pg/mL), the family requested withdrawal of ECMO and discharge against medical advice, and the child died 2 days post-discharge.
